title: Session SYN/ACK handshake, ack headers, affinity cookie, and graceful replay for streaming API
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Introduce a lightweight session-level SYN/ACK handshake and durable per-session metadata (session token, protocol flags, routing cookie) for the streaming text API so clients can reconnect with minimal rework and servers can offer graceful replay of recent output segments.

Motivation: Current reconnection logic relies on opaque client-side resume tokens and heuristics. We need an explicit session bootstrap that: 1) provides server routing affinity, 2) negotiates compression/format (json/event/line-delim), 3) publishes server-side retention window and max replay bytes, and 4) supplies a short-lifetime session token to authorize replay requests.

Design summary: Client issues an initial HTTP(S) GET with ?stream=1 and headers X-RW-SYN: <client-sid>, X-RW-PROTO: 1.2, optional X-RW-IF-HAS-KV: true. Server replies with a 200 SSE stream and a SYN-ACK block in the first event that includes: session_token, protocol_version, heartbeat_ms, replay_window_ms, affinity_cookie. Each data chunk emitted thereafter carries three headers in the SSE comment/metadata: rw-seq (monotonic semantic sequence id), rw-csum (crc32 of chunk payload), rw-cumulative-ack (server-provided cumulative offset). On reconnect the client presents session_token and last-acked rw-seq; server replies with SYN-ACK-REPLAY: starting_seq, available_bytes, and if within retention window, replays missing chunks before continuing live streaming.

Trade-offs considered: 1) We avoid full persistent connection guarantees (no server-side long-term durable logs) to keep storage cost low; retention window is bounded (default 2 minutes). 2) Using semantic sequence ids (not byte offsets) simplifies mismatched framing across clients but requires careful idempotency in downstream consumers. 3) Affinity cookie helps keep low-latency routing but increases cross-region failover complexity; fallback rules provided.

Operational concerns: eviction policy for cached chunks, memory caps per session, metrics for replay hit/miss, and per-tenant replay quotas. Security: session_token TTLs, KMS-backed signing for tokens for Private deployments, and explicit audit logging of replay actions.
acceptance_criteria: Client can establish a session and receive a SYN-ACK block with session_token, protocol_version, heartbeat_ms, and replay_window_ms
Server emits per-chunk metadata: rw-seq, rw-csum, and rw-cumulative-ack in the stream for every logical chunk
Client can reconnect with session_token and request replay from last acked rw-seq; server will replay cached chunks when within replay_window_ms
Replay path enforces per-tenant replay quota and logs audit events for replays
New protocol is backwards compatible: clients that ignore SYN-ACK metadata continue to work with best-effort reconnect heuristics
Performance: baseline median P50 token latency does not regress by more than 5% for synthetic chat workloads with session handshake enabled
discussion: 2025-02-14 - Aisha: Initial proposal posted; asking runtime and infra teams to weigh in on memory/eviction constraints.

2025-02-18 - Miguel: PoC for SYN/ACK block implemented in dev runtime. Uses in-memory ring buffer keyed by session_token with default retention 120s. Need infra opinion on cross-node routing for affinity cookie.

2025-02-20 - Lina (Infra): Affinity cookie will be set as HttpOnly Set-Cookie: rw_affinity=<node-hash>; expires in 3 minutes. Fallback: signed session_token can be used to route via control plane if cookie missing.
2025-02-22 - Security review notes: session_token must be signed and TTL <= 5 minutes; replay requests require explicit audit log entries and masking of PII in cached chunks for Private customers.

2025-02-26 - Design feedback from SDK team: prefer rw-seq as a string UUID for multi-part chunks; runtime team pushed back due to seq generation cost — settled on monotonic int per session with optional client-provided correlation id header.

2025-03-01 - Miguel: Integration tests covering normal connect, mid-stream reconnect, and replay after canonical ack are green locally. Filing PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/2189. Will request load test and perf run in next cycle.
